audit.whatIsWrong: diff is set to EVEN at a 56.38% Emerald+ win rate over 392 games, and the level chart gave six of seven stages to Tryndamere — a page that reads as a losing lane sitting on top of a clearly winning number.
audit.why: 56.38% is a favourable matchup, not an even one, and once the chart is corrected to match the whys[] (four stages Cho'Gath, one Tryndamere, two Skill) the EVEN label contradicts everything under it.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN -> FAV, tone -> #ff8b3d (the FAV colour this file uses elsewhere, e.g. the Ryze entry), and report[14].t reworded from 'Even matchup' to 'Favourable lane'. diffRating 7.5/10 left alone — the Ryze entry is FAV at 7.5 too, so difficulty and favourability are tracked separately here.

audit.why: The prose framing is right and always was: Tryndamere owns level 2-3 off Fury and Spinning Slash, Cho'Gath stabilises from 3 and takes over from 4-5 with Carnivore and Vorpal Spikes. Only the chart disagreed with the prose.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven stages contradict the page's own whys[] — every single one. whys[0] 'Level 1 is even' vs Tryndamere; whys[2] 'By level 3 it flattens out' vs Tryndamere; whys[3] 'Levels 4-5 swing to you' vs Tryndamere; whys[4] 'Level 6 is yours' vs Skill; whys[5] 'First item is yours' vs Tryndamere; whys[6] 'Late game is yours' vs Tryndamere. Only Level 2 was scored correctly.
audit.why: The packet chart matches all seven whys exactly and matches the 56.38% win rate. Mechanically Tryndamere has no armour shred and no true damage, so a Feast-stacked health pool is the one thing his crit autos cannot solve — the late stages are Cho'Gath's by kit, not by opinion.
audit.corrected: Level 1 Skill (5/10), Level 3 Skill (5/10), Levels 4-5 Cho'Gath (6/10), Level 6 Cho'Gath (6/10), First item Cho'Gath (6/10), 2+ items Cho'Gath (7/10). Proposed as one atomic chart group across both layers.

audit.whatIsWrong: Mocking Shout is described only as 'Mocking Shout's slow' — both of its actual properties are missing, and one of them is the single most actionable fact in the matchup. (a) It reduces surrounding champions' ATTACK DAMAGE, which directly guts Cho'Gath's Vorpal Spikes auto-attack damage. (b) The slow applies ONLY to enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere — walk toward him and there is no slow at all. The page instead teaches you to be kited by it. Second omission: Bloodlust passively increases Tryndamere's Attack Damage the more wounded he is, so chunking him makes him hit harder — nowhere on the page, despite the whole plan being a slow grind.
audit.why: Riot text — Mocking Shout: 'decreasing surrounding champions' Attack Damage. Enemies with their backs turned to Tryndamere also have their Move Speed reduced.' 14s flat, 850 range. Bloodlust: 'increasing his Attack Damage as he is more and more wounded. He can cast Bloodlust to consume his Fury and heal himself.' 12s flat, zero cost. Spinning Slash: 12/11/10/9/8s, 650 range, zero cost. Undying Rage: 120/100/80s, zero cost. Battle Fury: Fury raises his crit chance and is the fuel for the Bloodlust heal.
audit.corrected: The backs-turned condition and the AD cut written into dontsFull[2], report[5].t, phases[3].why, breakdown.cooldowns and wants.foe[1]; Bloodlust's wounded-AD scaling and Fury-to-heal conversion written into dosFull[1].d; Undying Rage's 120s rank-1 cooldown written into dosFull[0].d, phases[4].why and breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns named Undying Rage with no cooldown, and never mentioned Mocking Shout or Spinning Slash.
audit.why: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 — an enormous window once counted out — and Mocking Shout's 14s is what decides whether you can walk him down at all.
Plated Steelcaps plus early anti-heal is exactly right against a zero-resource crit auto-attacker whose only sustain is Bloodlust — the needs-antiheal entry the _missing file raises for this matchup.
'Never blow Feast before his Undying Rage timer is gone' is the correct and well-stated win condition — the one true-damage execute in the lane is dead weight against an ability that prevents death.

edits.before: Farm with E spikes and respect everything — you scale, he rents. Identify how Tryndamere contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Even at 1 — one ability each and no Fury banked yet, so neither can force. Deny his last-hits and set the wave for the level-2 window, which is his.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Tryndamere must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: It flattens out at 3 — Carnivore answers his chip and a landed Rupture into Feral Scream finally trades back even.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Undying Rage's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Your window: Carnivore and Vorpal Spikes out-sustain his Fury trades. Walk at him — Mocking Shout only slows a turned back.

edits.before: Feast stacks turn you into terrain — every R is permanent HP plus a true-damage execute. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Tryndamere's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is flat true damage his armour cannot touch, but Undying Rage refuses death outright — count the 120s R out or bait it before you spend yours.

edits.before: Heartsteel is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Undying Rage's cooldown.
edits.after: Heartsteel lands: your health lets you stand in his spin instead of being kited round it.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items on, Feast stacks outlast crit autos with no armour shred behind them. Your knockup peels his dive off your carries.

edits.before: Unkillable 5s. R-execute after it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Undying Rage is 120s at rank 1 — count it out or bait it, then Feast.

edits.before: Q under Tryndamere's feet as he commits, W-silence the answer, and E-spike the trade — your sustain regens what his chip cost.
edits.after: Bloodlust converts Fury into a heal and Battle Fury turns his missing health into AD — Grievous Wounds before you commit.

edits.before: Whiffing Q and fighting anyway — without the knockup your kit is a slow zone with no teeth.
edits.after: Its slow only lands on a turned back, and it cuts your AD — so walk at him, never away.

edits.before: Track Tryndamere's Undying Rage: Unkillable 5s. R-execute after it. When it is down — Q-W + R him.
edits.after: Mocking Shout cuts your AD and only slows a turned back. Undying Rage is 120s — Feast after it.

edits.before: - Tryndamere Undying Rage: matchup-defining — Unkillable 5s. R-execute after it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Tryndamere Undying Rage (120s at rank 1): matchup-defining — he cannot die through it, so count it out before you Feast. - Mocking Shout is 14s and only slows a turned back. - Feast: kill windows only.

edits.before: Even matchup — difficulty 7.5/10, Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10.
edits.after: Favourable lane — difficulty 7.5/10, Tryndamere carry threat 8.5/10.

edits.before: Spin-kite around your Rupture with Mocking Shout's slow and Spinning Slash resets so your skillshots whiff
edits.after: Get behind you so Mocking Shout's slow actually applies, then spin past Rupture with Spinning Slash

notes: All four packet suspectNames for this matchup are FALSE POSITIVES and I changed none of them: 'Build Fury' (Fury is his resource, correct usage), "Mocking Shout's" (possessive), 'Pop Undying Rage' (correct name with a verb), 'Spinning Slashes' (correct name used as a verb). UNVERIFIED, left in place: the page twice refers to 'Spinning Slash resets'. Riot's Data Dragon description for Spinning Slash says only 'slices toward a target unit, dealing damage to enemies in his path' — no crit-based cooldown reduction — but absence there is not a denial, so I neither leaned on the reset nor removed it. Also unverified and left alone: the '5s' duration attached to Undying Rage in several strings; the kit gives the cooldown (120/100/80) but no duration, so I used the cooldown in every line I rewrote and did not add or contradict the 5s figure. Note the tone change: flipping diff to FAV without also moving tone would leave the page rendering an even-lane colour on a favourable lane, so both are proposed together.
